problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [-6,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)=u(x-1)+u\,(x-\frac{1}{2})+u\,(x-\frac{1}{3})+⋯,\,g(x)=u(x+4)+u(x-6),\,h(x)={\begin{aligned}-1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is even} \\ 1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is odd}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌈x⌉$ is the ceiling function.

feedback.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [-5,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)=⌈x⌉,\,g(x)=u(x+1)+u(x+4),\,h(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡x
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌈x⌉$ is the ceiling function.
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose $I⊆R.$ A function $f:I\to R$ is piecewise continuous on $I$ if it is piecewise continuous on every closed and bounded subinterval $[a,b]⊂I.$

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [-5,\infty ).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=…,-2,-1,0,1,2,…,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]⊂[-5,\infty )$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14042449/assets/788b349598dcabebf92609183b3c48851d75bb11e22efff881a208e58be510b9.png)

- The function $g(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [-5,\infty )$ since it is continuous over $x\in [-5,\infty )$ except at the points $x=-4$ and $x=-1,$ where the one-sided limits exist and are finite:

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{4}^{-}}g(x)=0,\,{lim}_{x\to -{4}^{+}}g(x)=1
$$

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{1}^{-}}g(x)=1,\,{lim}_{x\to -{1}^{+}}g(x)=2
$$

- The function $h(x)$ is not piecewise continuous over $x\in [-5,\infty ).$ Consider the closed subinterval $x\in [0,\pi ].$ Notice that the one-sided limits at $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ are infinite:

$$
{lim}_{x\to \pi /{2}^{-}}h(x)=+\infty ,\,{lim}_{x\to \pi /{2}^{+}}h(x)=-\infty .
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$f$ and $g$ only."
